messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want my fair share of the house’s value, not to subsidize A’s purchase. I haven’t agreed to a discount. I don’t want to hurt my twin, but fairness matters too. I don’t know what a fair price or share is yet, and there’s no rush.
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband, if we can agree on a family discount. I know C hasn’t agreed, so nothing’s settled. I want the purchase to make sense for everyone.

Thank you. I’d like the estate to leave me with enough money to start a dance studio. I’m not sure what the right arrangement for the house is, especially since A would like to buy it and C hasn’t agreed.
Mostly. I want my fair share of the house’s value, and I don’t want to hurt my twin. I’m not in a rush, but I haven’t agreed to a discount.

That mostly fits. The house has family meaning, but the discount would make buying it more manageable for us and help us stand on our own financially. I can’t say everyone would feel good about it, especially since C hasn’t agreed.

It would let me build on my dance work and have a place of my own to teach. I don’t have a fixed deadline, but knowing roughly when funds might be available would help me plan. I’d change the summary to: “I want enough support from the estate to start a dance studio, with clarity about the amount and timing.”
Yes, that wording fits. An independent appraisal would help. I agree any plan should be based on the will, trusted facts, and everyone’s freely given agreement. I haven’t agreed to a discount.
Yes, that fits. I’m comfortable with checking the facts and making sure everyone freely agrees. I don’t want C to feel pressured; her agreement matters. Nothing else comes to mind right now.

Yes, I’m comfortable with everyone checking the facts and only agreeing freely. I don’t mind A buying the house in principle; I’d just want clarity about what it means for my share and when I could plan around it. And C’s agreement matters too.

Yes. A deadline shouldn’t be assumed or set until we know what the will and law allow; I’m not in a rush. And we need to verify how the inherited shares actually apply before saying A only finances the other two shares.

Yes. Full appraised value with no discount may make the purchase unaffordable; counting my share doesn’t necessarily make it manageable. I’d need to see the numbers before I could say whether financing would work.
Nothing major makes me uncomfortable. I’d just want the amount I could actually expect, and when, to be clear once the will and costs are checked. A realistic deadline would help too.
Yes, that feels fairer. I’ll share it with B and C. I still hope a discount can be considered, but I understand C hasn’t agreed and nothing is decided.
Yes, getting the will’s terms and an independent appraisal is fine. That’s not agreement to a discount; I still want my fair share.
